long_biography.plain_text:
Ivan Yakovlevich Streshinsky trained in applied mathematics and physics at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, graduating with honours. He joined Coalco early in his career and eventually became its chief executive after holding finance and operating posts. Work on the Gazmetall combination then placed him inside the group that developed Metalloinvest.

He became chief executive of Telecominvest in 2008 and took charge of USM when its owners consolidated their assets four years later. Alongside the holding-company role, Streshinsky served on boards overseeing mobile communications, mining, media and internet businesses. He received equity in two stages for his management contribution, bringing his holding to five percent. He left the chief-executive post in 2022 and departed the group’s main boards the following year, while retaining the stake that underpins his wealth.

uncertainties.detail: Forbes-derived Russian reporting directly names Ivan Streshinsky and his wife as Nataly S's owners and gives the same 38.36-metre length, 271-gross-ton volume, Custom Line builder and 2020 delivery as the authoritative input. SuperYacht Times independently validates the vessel, while keeping its owner field behind a subscription.

Ivan Yakovlevich Streshinsky is the stable public name used by Forbes, Kommersant and Interfax. MegaFon's annual report and OFAC identify Vladimir Yakovlevich Streshinskiy as a legal or alternate form and explicitly connect it to Ivan. The upstream display name is therefore preserved, and no unsupported name correction is proposed.

The input already gives the correct 2 October 1969 birth date but lists the Russian Federation as birth country. Kommersant and OFAC identify Kyiv as the birthplace, and OFAC explicitly gives Kyiv, Ukraine, supporting a correction to Ukraine under the current country taxonomy.

OFAC lists Israel and Cyprus as additional nationalities and documents passports for both. Because the owner schema offers only one secondary-nationality field and the current status of the cited Cyprus passport is unclear, neither is privileged in a proposal; both remain documented here for review.

Forbes continues to identify a five-percent USM stake, but Streshinsky left the chief-executive role in 2022 and the group's main boards in 2023. No strong current source identifies a renewed operating post, so Passive asset owner describes the present relationship while the biography preserves his historically defining operator role.

USM's portfolio includes major metals, mining, telecommunications, cement and technology assets, and Forbes itself summarizes Streshinsky's wealth as metals and telecom. No evidence demonstrates that one sector dominates his stake's value sufficiently to displace Diversified for either industry field.

The U.S. Treasury designated Streshinsky in April 2023, and his main USM board departures followed that month. The dossier records the official designation as identity and chronology evidence but does not speculate about conduct, motive or legal consequences, and it excludes the sanctions context from both publication biographies.

Forbes provides current net-worth estimates and recent dividend rankings, but these values change and are not needed to explain the wealth mechanism. The dossier states the continuing five-percent stake without importing a dollar valuation, transaction price or dividend total.

The existing Forbes Russia, LinkedIn and Instagram profiles align with the exact person. No separate personal website, Facebook, X, YouTube or TikTok profile met the proposal threshold, and the newer global Forbes page is recorded in forbes_profile rather than duplicating the existing Forbes social.

USM is assigned because Streshinsky was its long-term chief executive, led major portfolio boards and retains a material minority stake. Metalloinvest, Mobile telecommunications and Iron ore mining were considered but omitted as redundant subordinate expressions of the same diversified USM relationship.

review.notes:
Review Diversified / Diversified / Self-made / Passive asset owner. Ivan Yakovlevich Streshinsky resolves conclusively through direct Nataly S attribution matching the input's exact dimensions and delivery year, supported by Forbes, Kommersant, Interfax, corporate reports and OFAC across his patronymic and Vladimir legal-name variant. His fortune arose when USM's owners awarded him a five-percent stake for long-term executive management; the multi-sector holding remains his principal identifiable wealth after his executive and board departures. The dossier proposes a known-for title, Kyiv birthplace, Ukraine birth-country correction and a vessel-independent biography. It preserves the current public name, does not select between two additional nationalities, and excludes net-worth estimates and sanctions commentary from publication copy. Nothing has been compiled, approved or applied.

Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] USM: A decade as chief executive, major portfolio chairmanships and continuing five-percent ownership satisfy the approved company-affiliation contract as a genuinely defining long-term leader. [2] Metalloinvest: Streshinsky's chairmanship was substantial, but a separate company tag is omitted because it is subordinate to the assigned USM identity. [3] Mobile telecommunications and Iron ore mining: Both sectors materially shaped his career and stake, yet assigning each would fragment a demonstrably diversified holding-company mechanism and duplicate the USM tag.
